discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron spins in solid-state defects, establishing a platform for quantum sensing and quantum networks
subfield: Quantum optics and solid-state quantum technologies
motivation: Wrachtrup, Awschalom and Lukin turned an individual point defect in a crystal, the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, into a controllable quantum system at room temperature. Wrachtrup pioneered optically detected magnetic resonance and coherent control of single defect spins. Awschalom demonstrated fast coherent manipulation and dynamics of single spins in diamond and extended defect spin physics to technologically mature materials such as silicon carbide. Lukin showed that coupled electron and nuclear spins form long-lived quantum registers and conceived nanoscale magnetometry with single spins. Together their work created a new field: single-spin quantum sensors now image magnetism, currents and biological processes at the nanoscale, and defect spin-photon interfaces underpin the first multi-node quantum networks. This discovery exemplifies how control of a single quantum system reveals new physics and delivers broad technological impact across condensed matter, biology and quantum information.
